name: argilcad-mcp

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Whether a project is open, whether the CAD engine is ready and whether a model is on screen.

tools.name: get_modeling_guide
tools.description: The rules a build123d script must follow to run in ArgilCAD, with an example. Read it once before writing code.

tools.name: get_code
tools.description: The build123d script in the open project's editor, including the user's own unsaved edits.

tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Run a complete build123d script (it must assign `result`). Replaces the code in the user's editor, shows the model in their ArgilCAD window and adds a step to the project timeline, which they can undo. Returns size, volume and parts — with their colours, materials and joints as the Studio will show them — or the error and traceback. Problems with `studio` come back as warnings.

code.description: The whole Python script. Units are millimetres.

description.description: A few words for the timeline step, in the user's language.

tools.name: get_model_info
tools.description: Size, volume and parts of the model on screen. Part ids, labels and names here are what export_model and create_drawing take.

tools.name: render_view
tools.description: A PNG of the model on screen from a standard view, so you can see what you built — in its colours and materials once it has any. Does not move the user's camera or change what they see.

look.description: materials: the Studio's colours and materials; plain: one flat colour, for reading the shape. Default auto: materials once the model has colours.

pose.description: Joints to turn for this still, by name (degrees, or mm for a prismatic joint), e.g. {"lid": 90}; the rest stay as modelled.

time.description: For a model with studio["animation"]: the moment to show, in seconds. The camera frames everywhere the parts go.

tools.name: check_motion
tools.description: Works every joint of the model on screen through its range, and its animation through its run, and lists the parts that run into each other, with the joint value (or the second of the animation) where they first do. Joints and animation come from `studio` in the code, or the Studio. Does not change what the user sees.

tools.name: export_model
tools.description: Save the model on screen as STEP, STL, 3MF or GLB — into the project folder on the desktop, or as a download in the browser.

part.description: Export only this part (id, label or name from get_model_info).

tools.name: prepare_print
tools.description: Get the model on screen ready to 3D print: laid out on the printer's bed, turned onto the face that prints best, each part on the filament of its Studio colour, saved as a 3MF. Parts laid out apart that one plate cannot hold go onto more, a 3MF each (`plates`). On the desktop the first then opens in the user's slicer (Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer, Creality Print, PrusaSlicer…), where they slice and print with their own profiles; in a browser it downloads. Returns what the layout found: size, parts too big or too tall for the printer, the area printed over air (may need supports), the filaments, and `print_check` — walls, holes and gaps too small for the nozzle, each with the `min_mm` to fix it to in the code. Settings not given come from the Studio's print section; the ones given apply to this call only. Nothing is sliced or sent to a printer.

printer.description: The user's printer. Default: the one chosen in ArgilCAD's Studio. "custom" needs bed_mm.

bed_mm.description: Width, depth and height in mm of a printer not in the list.

orient.description: auto turns the model onto the face that prints best; asis prints it standing as modelled. Default: the Studio's.

arrange.description: For several parts: together keeps them assembled (hinges, print-in-place); apart lays each out on its best face. Default: the user's choice in the Studio, else the code's `studio["print"]["arrange"]`, else ArgilCAD decides — together when some parts are held in one another across print-in-place clearances (`printed_in_place` in the reply), apart otherwise.

open_in_slicer.description: Open it in the slicer found on the user's computer. Default true.

open_plate.description: Of several plates, the one to open in the slicer. Default 1.

save.description: false lays the model out and checks it without saving a file or opening a slicer: for checking again after a fix. Default true.

nozzle.description: Nozzle width in mm, which the print check measures walls and holes against. Default: the Studio's.

skip.description: Parts left out of the print — bought rather than printed (screws, bearings, glass). Default: the Studio's list.

split.description: Cut a part no plate holds into pieces that fit. Default: the Studio's (on).

connector.description: What joins cut pieces: printed pins in blind holes, or glue alone. Default: the Studio's (pin).

pack.description: Parts laid out apart: fewest plates, or each subassembly on its own plates. Default: the Studio's.

one_color_per_plate.description: Each plate in one filament, for a printer without an AMS or CFS. Default: the Studio's.

supports.description: Turn supports on in the file for a part printing over air. Default: the Studio's (on).

brims.description: Turn a brim on in the file for a part that may tip. Default: the Studio's (on).

booklet.description: Also save the assembly booklet: an HTML page per subassembly numbering every printed item and its plate.

tools.name: set_appearance
tools.description: Change how parts look in the user's Studio: a material from the Studio's library, a colour, a finish, the environment. Saved with the project as the user's own choice over the code's look — not a timeline step. Use it only when the user asks to try a look in the Studio; a look that belongs to the model goes in the code's `studio["appearance"]`. Returns every part's look and whose it is.

part.description: A part's name, an assembly's label (all its parts), or "*" for every part without a look of its own.

color.description: "#RRGGBB". Left out, the material keeps the colour it can carry over.

reset.description: Parts given back the code's look (or the default); "*" for all.

environment.description: The light and background. photo_studio, workshop and outdoor are photographs, with Starter and Pro.

tools.name: render_photo
tools.description: A path-traced photo of the model in the user's Studio — its materials, light and environment — saved like the Studio's own (downloaded in a browser). Switches the user's window to the Studio and draws there, so use it only when the user asks for a picture or a render; render_view is for checking your work. Returns a smaller copy to look at.

view.description: current keeps the user's camera. Default current.

quality.description: draft is quick; standard and high take minutes on a large image. Default draft.

size.description: The long edge: 1920, 2560 or 3840 px. 4K is Pro. Default hd.

dimensions.description: Paint the dimensions the user pinned over it.

tools.name: record_video
tools.description: An MP4 of the model in the user's Studio, made on their computer and saved like the Studio's own (downloaded in a browser): the model turning, its parts coming together, or its joints and animation at work. Switches the user's window to the Studio, so use it only when the user asks for a video.

scene.description: turntable: turning once round. assemble: the parts coming together (several parts). mechanism: the joints or the animation at work. Default turntable.

aspect.description: 16:9 for a page, 1:1 for a feed, 9:16 for Reels and Shorts. Default 16:9.

resolution.description: The short edge. 4K is Pro. Default 720p.

dimensions.description: Paint the dimensions the user pinned over every frame.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: The user's ArgilCAD projects, newest first, and which one is open.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Open one of the user's projects by name. Switches the user's window, so do it only when no project is open or the user asked for that project.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new project and open it, ready for run_code. Use it when no project is open, or when the user wants a new one. Name it after the part, briefly, in the user's language.

tools.name: create_drawing
tools.description: Make an A4 technical drawing (SVG) of the model on screen, saved like an export.

part.description: Draw only this part (id, label or name).

tools.name: show_in_argilcad
tools.description: Bring the ArgilCAD window to the front so the user sees the model. Call it once, without asking, when you have finished a model or a change to it (after your last run_code and review), and whenever the user asks to see it. It takes the user's focus: never in the middle of your work.

instructions: ArgilCAD is a parametric CAD app built on build123d (Python). Read get_modeling_guide before writing code; a script must assign `result`. Work happens in an open project: if none is open, create_project one. run_code shows the model in the user's ArgilCAD window and adds it to the project timeline, where the user can undo it. Check your work with render_view, and fix errors from the traceback run_code returns. If a tool answers that ArgilCAD is not connected, pass on to the user what it says to do; the tools work as soon as ArgilCAD connects.
